A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LAD-RAG work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original retrieval and QA experiments on four benchmarks, component ablations, case studies, and inference-overhead analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these experiments and adds RAPTOR comparisons, document-type results, and a human validation study of automated QA scoring.

M1.justification: The ingestion pipeline, running memory, symbolic graph, neural index, and three agent retrieval operations are unchanged. All four prompt templates are retained. Newly discussed preliminary extraction checks do not replace GPT-4o or alter the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MMLongBench-Doc, LongDocURL, DUDE, and MP-DocVQA on the same retrieval and QA tasks. The new document-type breakdown and human audit examine existing benchmark coverage; discussion of scanned documents does not establish a new test scenario.

E2.justification: V2 adds RAPTOR as an evaluated hierarchical retriever in Figures 3 and 7 and Table 1. Existing retrieval baselines and QA comparison models remain. References to SimpleDoc and M3DocRAG do not constitute additional evaluated systems.

E3.justification: New Appendix G introduces a human-validation protocol: 100 MMLongBench-Doc answers, balanced between automated correct/incorrect labels, independently assessed by two annotators. The established benchmark metrics, decoding settings, and retrieval-budget comparisons remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds QA analysis across seven document types, validation of automated judging, and qualitative observations about scans and InternVL2-8B versus GPT-4o extraction. Existing component ablations, case studies, and evidence-type analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 6 newly reports human–judge and inter-annotator agreement using accuracy and Cohen’s kappa. This adds statistical reliability assessment, but neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty or confidence intervals for the main benchmark results.

E6.justification: Added results include RAPTOR’s Table 1 scores of 0.877 and 0.853, document-type scores in Table 5, and agreement scores in Table 6. Average baseline retrieval depths change from 25 to 22 and 29 to 27 with RAPTOR included. Existing QA values in Tables 2–4 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The definitions of perfect recall and irrelevant-pages ratio are unchanged. Neither version introduces theoretical assumptions, theorems, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations beyond the retained formulation.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about layout-aware document graphs, adaptive retrieval, retrieval completeness, QA gains, and low inference overhead. The added introduction paragraph elaborates existing human-reading motivation.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of RAPTOR comparisons and document-type differences, an explanation for occasionally outperforming ground-truth-evidence QA, and more specific discussion of scan quality, model selection, and computational tradeoffs. These refine the existing interpretation and limitations without redefining the work’s scope.

D1.justification: The implementation appendix moves from G to H while retaining the same software, hardware, hyperparameters, image-rendering procedure, and prompt templates. Appendix A still states that public code release awaits institutional review and legal clearance.

R1.justification: V2 adds Béchard and Ayala (2024) and sharpens comparisons with previously cited work, particularly RAPTOR’s semantic hierarchy, SimpleDoc’s dynamic retrieval, and the computational costs of other systems. The overall research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: V2 adds introductory motivation, expands results interpretation, related work, and limitations, and inserts a human-evaluation appendix. The main section order and most existing prose remain; terminology and citation corrections are limited.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 5–6, a RAPTOR row in Table 1, and RAPTOR curves and legend entries in Figures 3 and 7. Existing displays are reflowed, including moving Figure 9 onto a separate page, while the overall visual format is retained.

improvement.justification: The RAPTOR comparison, document-type analysis, and human scoring validation strengthen empirical support beyond v1. Table 6 reports 93–95% human–judge agreement, providing useful evidence for evaluation reliability. The gain is limited: the audit covers only 100 LAD-RAG answers from one benchmark, and added causal and cost explanations remain largely qualitative. The central method and existing QA results are unchanged.
